Maya R.: Filing this here — customer (AcmePayments) says the traces UI shows the request ID but no spans after the gateway hop. request id: `req_7f3a9b` :thinking_face:
Elaine (CS): Customer opened a support ticket, attaching screenshots and a sample request id. They see a greyed-out trace timeline and a little ‘no spans found’ message under the span list. Ticket: #ACME-6789
Maya R.: Does anyone know if we recently changed the request-id -> trace-id correlation logic? I can repro locally but only when the client sends `X-Req-Id` (capitalization) instead of `x-request-id`.
Sam I.: I grabbed exporter logs for that timeframe. Looks like several spans were received by the collector but later dropped at the linking stage:
```
2026-11-02T14:02:11Z WARN linking: missing_parent_ref span=svc-b.process span_id=0x3f1 parent_ref="" request_id=req_7f3a9b
2026-11-02T14:02:11Z DEBUG sampler: sampler decision=keep span_id=0x3f1
2026-11-02T14:02:11Z INFO linker: failed to attach span span_id=0x3f1 -> trace_id= (empty)
```
Sam I.: The collector expects parent_ref to be a 16-byte hex string. If instrumentation emits an empty string we treat it as malformed and drop the link. That leaves an orphaned span in the raw store but not attached to a trace timeline.
Luis (eng-runtime): This smells like the recent auto-instrumentation change that tried to normalise header names. If the SDK rewrites header keys but leaves parent_id blank for some child spans, the linker loses the chain.
Elaine (CS): Customer says this started after a deploy last week. They can repro consistently with a specific endpoint: `POST /payments/process` with header `X-Req-Id: req_7f3a9b`.
Maya R.: Repro steps requested by eng:
1) curl -v -X POST https://api.acme.example/payments/process -H "X-Req-Id: req_7f3a9b" -d '{"amt":10}'
2) set DEBUG_TRACING=1 on the gateway pod to capture raw spans
3) query collector for request_id `req_7f3a9b` and inspect raw spans via `GET /internal/traces/raw?request_id=req_7f3a9b`
Maya R.: I ran this locally and saw the same pattern — spans from svc-a are present but service-b emits spans with `parent_ref: ""` so they become unlinked.
Sam I.: Quick mitigation: change linker to tolerate empty parent_ref by falling back to request_id-based stitching for a short window (30s) while we patch SDK. I'll open a PR with the safe fallback and add metrics to measure how often it fires. :hammer_and_wrench:
Luis (eng-runtime): If we add fallback, please ensure we only use it when trace_id is missing and request_id matches, to avoid accidentally linking unrelated traces. Also add a feature flag for rollout.
Maya R.: Customer update: asking for ETA because this affects payments history for a small subset of requests.
Elaine (CS): I told them we're investigating and that eng will try a hotfix. They asked for a temporary dashboard query to surface orphaned spans — can someone add a saved search? Query should look for `parent_ref = "" AND service = "svc-b"` in raw spans.
Luis (eng-runtime): I'll add the saved search and a short alert (ops -> oncall) if orphaned span count > 5/min. Also creating GH issue: runtime#1423 referencing this thread.
tracing-bot: New issue created runtime#1423 by Luis (eng-runtime). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/issues/1423 :link:
Sam I.: Follow-up actions I will take:
- PR: linker fallback + feature flag (target: patch release tomorrow)
- Instrumentation repo: add validation to never emit empty parent_ref; fall back to omitting the field instead of empty-string (longer-term fix)
- Add unit tests that round-trip parent/child linkages with various header capitalizations
Maya R.: Thanks all. Elaine, I'll draft an interim customer message: "We see the spans arriving but some child spans have malformed parent IDs after a recent SDK normalization. We're rolling a safe fallback to preserve links while we fix SDKs; ETA 24-36h." :thumbsup:
Elaine (CS): Sounds good. I'll update ticket #ACME-6789 and ping the customer.
Maya R.: Please keep me posted here when PRs are merged or if we need a rollback option.
Luis (eng-runtime): Noted. Will post PR/rollout plan in this thread. :eyes:
